deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is continuous German prose in a student or lecture-notes style, carried over from fol. 91 and continuing on the next page. It narrates Greek history during the Peloponnesian War, roughly 413–411 BC.

1. End of the Sicilian expedition (413): the Athenians try to reach an allied city, but the Syracusans block the road and the whole army surrenders the next morning. One commander was apparently executed and the other perished. The troops were partly killed and partly enslaved.
2. Alcibiades in Sparta: he quickly gains influence, and on his advice the war is formally resumed. He persuades the Spartans to fortify and garrison Decelea in Attica, from where raids keep the Athenians nearly confined to their city.
3. Persia: he draws the Persians in and opens contact with the satrap Tissaphernes, which worsens Athens' position.
4. Fall in Sparta: his immorality makes him hated there, and he barely escapes by flight, going to Tissaphernes in 411. He now plans to regain a role in Athens.
5. Athens after Sicily: despite the defections of allies, the Athenians keep a reserve of 1000 talents, build a new fleet, and put to sea to punish the defectors.
6. Alcibiades then tries to win Tissaphernes for the Athenian side, arguing that it is not in Persia's interest for Sparta to gain complete supremacy. The sentence breaks off with 'Tissaphernes ging in die' and continues on the next page.

The text corresponds to standard early-19th-century German university history lectures, of the Heeren/Göttingen type. The hand and content suggest notes, possibly not by Gauss himself, bound in this bundle. There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors.

Chronology: the dates in the text deviate from the standard chronology. Alcibiades fled to Sparta in 415. The fortification of Decelea was in 413, not 414. The formal renewal of open war came in 414/413. The '415' attached to the renewal of the war, if correctly read, is wrong.
Fate of the commanders: both Athenian commanders, Nicias and Demosthenes, were executed by the Syracusans. The text has one executed and the other perished, if the reading is correct.
Tissaphernes: Alcibiades' flight to Tissaphernes is usually dated 412, not 411.

results.what: Narrative notes on the end of the Sicilian expedition, Alcibiades in Sparta and with Tissaphernes, the fortification of Decelea, and Athens' recovery (c. 413–411 BC)
results.modern_name: Lecture notes on ancient Greek history (Peloponnesian War)
results.usually_credited_to: Thucydides (primary source); standard material in 18th/19th-century German history lectures (e.g., A. H. L. Heeren at Göttingen)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine historical lecture or study notes on the Peloponnesian War, with no mathematical content. Even if written by Gauss, such notes would be of only biographical interest.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: 'de[?] Feigherzigste[?]' is more plausibly 'hingerichtet', giving 'Einer von ihren Anführern war hingerichtet, der andere war umgekommen'. This matches the parallel 'umgekommen' and the historical execution of the commanders.
Line 5: 'zum Theil nieder' is likely elliptical for 'niedergemacht', completed by the shared verb 'gemacht'.

Insertion and next line: the marginal insertion is '+ Alcibiades, in', keyed to the cross after 'stürzte sich'. The garbled 'te[?] selbst' is likely the end of a word split across the line, plausibly '[Spar]ta selbst', giving 'Indessen stürzte sich Alcibiades in Sparta selbst'. This is uncertain.
'machte ihn verhaßt in Sparta / er konnte sich' should probably read 'machte ihn verhaßt, und er konnte sich kaum noch durch die Flucht retten'.
'daß sein Interesse gar[?] nicht wenn[?] Sparta' probably reads 'daß es für sein Interesse gar nicht wäre, wenn Sparta das völlige Übergewicht erhielt'.
'allein die Syrakuser aber besetzten' is correctly read; the redundancy of 'allein ... aber' is in the original.
'und erschienen wieder in See, und die abgefallenen' is probably 'um die abgefallenen Bundesgenossen zu züchtigen' ('und' misread for 'um').
